## Summary
Implements **P08.3 — Contradiction as a first-class object** (canonical §31, §28.7),
stacked on P08.2. `Contradiction` becomes a materialized entity with a full lifecycle,
a manual publication brake, a publish-not-hide projection, and a byte-identical L3
rebuild gate.

- **Materialized entity (SIG-RECON-053).** Promotes the existing
  `reconcile.model.Contradiction` (additive, back-compat — all call-sites keyword) into
  the stored §31 shape: its own identity (`contradiction_id`), the disagreeing
  `claim_ids[]`, and resolution fields (`resolution_note`/`resolved_by`/`resolved_at`)
  alongside the pre-existing `severity`/`status`/`research_task_ids`.
- **Lifecycle (SIG-RECON-056).** `open → under_research → resolved /
  accepted_unresolvable / superseded`, with `accepted_unresolvable` a legitimate
  terminal state. Append-only transition methods return **new** records — never edited
  in place (SIG-RECON-021).
- **The manual brake (SIG-RECON-054).** An open `severity = blocking` contradiction
  forces the resolver to `UNRESOLVED` (`U7`) via `contradiction.forces_unresolved` —
  it stops publication without deleting anything.
- **Publishable, not hidden (SIG-RECON-055).** An open contradiction surfaces as
  `unresolved_conflict` in `publishable_view`/`Contradiction.public_view` and via the
  resolution's `contradiction_state`; a resolved one stays visible in history.
- **Byte-identical L3 rebuild (SIG-RECON-019/020/021).** `reconcile.rebuild` reruns the
  resolver and asserts the fresh `input_digest` + full decision key match; a committed
  `data/l3_rebuild_sample.json` is regenerated and asserted in CI; a version change is
  refused as `NonReproducible`.
- **Detector→task contract (SIG-RECON-057).** Enforced uniformly across every detector
  (the §29 workflows and the resolver's Phase-2 guards); `counts` now links its
  disagreement task and the resolver emits **deterministic** research tasks so the
  record stays reproducible.

Spec: `docs/tickets/P08.3__contradiction-object.md`. Design + deviations: **ADR-037**.

## What changed
- `reconcile/model.py` — `Contradiction` promoted to the materialized entity + lifecycle;
  `CountResolution` gains an additive `tasks` field.
- `reconcile/contradiction.py` *(new)* — `materialize`, `forces_unresolved`,
  `publishable_view`, `detector_task_violations`/`assert_detector_task_contract`.
- `reconcile/rebuild.py` *(new)* + `reconcile/data/l3_rebuild_sample.json` *(new)* — the
  byte-identical rebuild + committed CI sample.
- `reconcile/resolve.py` — Phase-2 contradictions emit deterministic linked tasks;
  `Resolution` gains an additive `tasks` field.
- `reconcile/counts.py` — value_disagreement contradiction links its research task.
- Tests *(new)*: `test_contradiction.py`, `test_detector_task_contract.py`,
  `test_rebuild.py`.
- Docs: `ADR-037`, traceability matrix (§31/§28.7), risk register (RISK-P8-10..14).

## Design decisions
- The entity is modelled in **pure Python** aligned with
  `db/deploy/graph_annotations.sql`, **not** persisted to Postgres here — continuing the
  ADR-031/036 precedent; the read-API endpoint is P14.1 (out of scope). Persistence is a
  downstream wiring step.
- The existing `Contradiction` is **promoted** rather than duplicated into a second type.
- The byte-identical rebuild is verified **in-process** against the resolver; the sample
  is the CI reproducibility gate (regenerate deliberately when ruleset/resolver bump).
- `reconcile_as_single_count` / `count_basis_mismatch` are refusal/demonstration helpers
  (P08.2), not lifecycle detectors; the real `predicate_conflation` **detector** (resolver
  Phase 2.3) emits a task, so the §31 contract holds on the detection path.
